solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S013-01.notes: 'leaving reporters unsure whether she supported it' defines equivocal; candid/vehement contradict the uncertainty, belated is off-topic. Difficulty comes from the vocabulary word itself.

S013-02.notes: Text 2 raises self-selection bias, so she would question generalizing to firms that did not volunteer. B contradicts the data, C overgeneralizes, D is unsupported.

S013-03.notes: Only C shows both a stern exterior (scowled) and hidden generosity (secretly left bread). B shows sternness only; D shows open generosity.

S013-04.notes: A restrictive clause is needed to say which of the two portraits is meant, so 'that hangs' takes no commas. B is nonrestrictive and lacks a closing comma, C puts a comma between subject and verb, and D uses a comma before 'that'.

S013-05.notes: Compound predicate (tested ... and replaced) with one subject takes no comma. A puts an unneeded comma before the second verb, B misuses a semicolon, and C creates a comma splice.

S013-06.notes: The second sentence offers a counterpoint to the critics, so a contrast is needed. Similarly, For this reason and In other words all signal continuation.

S013-07.notes: Village seems larger/emptier, bakery shuttered, square paved; fountain is the only thing she recognized. A and C contradict, D is unsupported.

flags: minor: C is the longest and most data-dense choice and the only one that compares across modes, a mild test-wise tell
S013-08.notes: The claim compares percentage-point growth across modes, so the answer must give cycling's +8 and show it beats the others. Only walking (+3) also grew, and C states both. A (more than doubled) is a relative-change trap. B and D give data for only one other mode.

S013-09.notes: Starch that was heated before grinding implies a multi-step process (heating/drying, then grinding). B contradicts 'long before domestication', C overreaches, and D contradicts the oat starch. Consistent with the real Grotta Paglicci finding (~32,000 years ago).

S013-10.notes: The text gives two competing views and then a study showing repetition matters for nouns and context for verbs, so the finding partly supports each view.
